question: How can probability theory give a principled basis for ranking documents by likelihood of relevance, and what term weights (BIM, BM25) follow?
contributions: Binary Independence Model derivation of RSV and ct weights (11.3)
BM25 forms (11.4.3), tree dependencies, Bayesian networks

results.claim: k1=0 gives a binary model; large k1 approaches raw term frequency; b=1 is full length normalisation, b=0 none.
results.quote: A k1 value of 0 corresponds to a binary model (no term frequency), and a large value corresponds to using raw term frequency.

results.claim: Probabilistic IR historically never won on performance; BM25 in the 1990s changed that.
results.quote: Traditionally, probabilistic IR has had neat ideas but the methods have never won on performance.

results.claim: Under the assumption that relevant documents are a tiny fraction of the collection, ut = df_t/N, so log((1-ut)/ut) ~ log N/df_t, a theoretical justification for idf.
results.setup: BIM, Eq 11.22, relevant docs approximated as negligible
results.quote: In other words, we can provide a theoretical justiﬁcation for the most frequently used form of idf weighting

results.claim: Croft and Harper constant pt = 0.5 makes ranking equal to the sum of idf over query terms present.
results.setup: BIM, constant pt over all query terms; suited to short documents (titles, abstracts) without iterative searching
results.quote: For instance, we might assume that pt is constant over all terms xt in the query and that pt = 0.5.

results.claim: Greiff proposed pt = 1/3 + 2/3 df_t/N because pt rises with df_t.
results.setup: BIM probability estimate for pt; plausible proposal from Greiff's data analysis
results.quote: a plausible proposal would be to use the estimate pt = 1
results.note: Text prints 'pt = 1' then '3 + 2/3 dft/N' split across lines (extraction layout); the quote is truncated at the line break.

results.claim: Bayesian update of pt uses prior weight kappa of about 5 when the user judges roughly 5 documents.
results.setup: Relevance feedback, Eq 11.25, user judging about 5 documents
results.quote: a value of around κ = 5 is perhaps appropriate

results.claim: Relevance feedback may expand the query with some 10-20 top terms of known relevant documents, ranked by c-hat_t.

results.quote: (say, 10–20) of the top terms in the known-relevant documents

results.claim: The idf variant log((N-df+1/2)/(df+1/2)) goes negative when a term is in over half the documents; floor at 0 or use a stop list.
results.quote: if a term occurs in over half the documents in the collection then this model gives a negative term weight

results.claim: PRP is optimal (minimises Bayes risk) under 1/0 loss only if all probabilities are known correctly, which never holds in practice.
results.quote: However, it requires that all probabilities are known correctly. This is never the case in practice.

results.claim: BIM is identical to multivariate Bernoulli Naive Bayes and assumes term independence, which is far from correct but often works.
results.quote: This assumption is far from correct, but it nevertheless often gives satisfactory results in practice

results.claim: BIM was designed for short catalogue records and abstracts of consistent length; full text needs tf and length handling.

limits: No experiments or data: every number is a recommended default or a worked equation.
BM25 defaults (k1 1.2-2, b 0.75) attributed to unnamed 'experiments'; no collection, metric or citation at that point.
BM25 full theory not developed; defers to Spärck Jones et al. 2000 and Robertson 2005.
2008 text: predates dense retrieval, learned sparse retrieval and neural rerankers; says language models (Ch 12) are the recent success; Bayesian-network IR said to have little follow-on.
practices: When no relevance data exist, score with idf (Eq 11.30) or the 1/2-smoothed variant (Eq 11.31) with a floor of 0 (11.4.3).
Tune k1, k3 and b on a separate development test collection by grid search or better; otherwise k1,k3 in 1.2-2 and b=0.75 (11.4.3).
Skip query length normalisation and, for short queries, query tf weighting (k3 term) (11.4.3).
In pseudo-relevance feedback guess a conservative (too small) relevant set, e.g. fixed top-|V| documents (11.3.4).
Smooth pt estimates and combine with the prior via Bayesian updating, kappa about 5 (11.3.4).

terms.definition: rank documents in decreasing order of probability of relevance P(R=1|d,q)
documents and queries are binary term incidence vectors; terms occur independently
RSV_d = sum over query terms present in d of ct, the log odds ratio
ratio of the odds of a term appearing in relevant vs nonrelevant documents; ct is its log
Simultaneously decreasing the estimated probability of seen events and increasing the probability of unseen events
Okapi weighting: probabilistic model sensitive to tf and document length with few extra parameters
you lose a point for returning a nonrelevant or failing to return a relevant document
